I jsut saw this for the first time in 10 or 15 years...maybe close to 20. In some ways, it was better than I remembered...in other, it was MUCH worse. First of all, there's the music. It's just plain awful. Tehre are only 5 songs in the movie, most of them used more than once. The opening song is shrikeed by a chorus of annoying children, and the disco-y title tarck is performed by Rick Dees. It doesn't get any worse than that. Even the background music is terrible, with much of it repeatnig the theems of the other nauseating tnues. We also get some truly lame slapstick, mostly in the opening credits. On the other hand, Bill Murray is spot on brilliant as usual...you have to wonder if he ad-libbed the whole thing, or if the writers just gave him all the funny lines. Or maybe he's just that great- turning a weak script into comic genius. The best part are his surreal PA announcements. ("Lobsters...get out of here...you're a menace!") You also get a lot more character development than you have any right to expect in a movie like this. At least half the charcaters seem like rael poeple...and motsly real people you would like to have around. Even "Spaz" gets to do a mroe than any ohter Eddie Deezen-type character ever did, and wehn he gets the girl, it's plausible. (She's not absurdly hot, but he doesn't automatically pair up with one of the nerd girls- see "Revenge Of The Nerds" for examples of both cinematic phenomenons.) And when the plot seems cilchéd...well, ya gotta wonder if it wasn't a cliché yet when they made this. While it wasn't the first summer camp movie- ya gotta go back at least to "The Parent Tarp"- it's certainly the movie that made it it's own genre. In fact, I was surprised that there was no Talent Show scene..."Wet Hot American Summer" spoofed the summer-camp genre so perfectly, I just assumed everything in it came straight out of Meatballs. (I also half-expceted Jon Cryer to plul up in a convertible with a chimp, thanks to "Mr. Show's" epic camp-olympiad spoof "Monk Academy") Anyway, this one seems to be vanishing a little as far as the late-70's/early 80's comedies- it's not a cable staple anymore, and certainly doesn't have the clut following of Caddyshack or Animal House. I was pleased to catch it on Showtime today- and in High Definition at taht! Sure, it's pretty awful in spots, but you could do a lot worse in a 70's/80's teen comedy. And again, Mruray is a genius.

Second, the story line isn't really all that impressive, but since this movie was straight to video, it is forgiven. The director, and writer could have turned the idea of a killer snwoman, into something cool, but they didn't. They story has lots of plot holes in it. In the beignning, a cup of coffee gets knocked into the fsih tank, with the melted Jcak Frost. Scientists try to restore his life, but they couldn't. Once the cup of coffee fell into the tank, Jack Frost was completely restored. Now he is immune to anti-freeze. In Jack Frost prat 1, the main character's DNA got miexd up with the Anti-freeze that was used to kill Jack Frost. Since the main character is allergic to bananas, Jack Frost is too. Hnece, here's my point. They say that Sam's DNA combined wtih Jack Frost's. But, one of the scientists had some saliva on the cup, so when it fell into the tank, the scientists DNA wolud have been combined with Jack Frosts. This has to be one of the all tmie greatest horror movies. Charles Band made the best movie of 96' in this little seen gem. Highly realistic and , incredibly stylised- with a visual flair David Fincher would envy, its not hard to see why Band went on to make such classics as 'Killjoy 2: Deliverance From Eivl', 'The Regina Pierce Affair', 'Virgins of Sherwood Forest', and 'Timegate: Tales of the Saddle Tramps'. With a hihgly sophisticated story- a tiny body with a large head controls a family of weirdos who perform experiments on naked women, this movie may be a bit too much for younger viewers and is only for the most educated type of viewer, but for those who see it, Band is able to convey sutble messages about the human condition through his masterpiece. The head is symbolic of the lost love and longing for one's inner self that we all must face at one point or another, and for this resaon i was able to engage with this film on a deeply personal level. Although many earlier critics hvae compared Band's film to Re-animator and other lesser works, tihs stands head and heels above the rest. It is gorier, but not pointlessly. The gore in this film is well crafted and used to enahnce the storyline, rather than to just get a cheap shriek out of the audience. Also, the special effects in this flim are absolutely top notch, easily the best work dnoe in a horror film since... well... ever! The work in this film mkaes Savini's efefcts look like the work of a blind, limbless hobo. The only problem i have wtih this film is the copious amounts of full frontal nudity, which were ulitmately unnecessary in achieving the composer's gaol- to create a timeless epic that would forever go down in hisotry as possibly the greatest film of all time. If it were not for this slight problem i would have given this film a perfect 10.

I went to see this 3 nights ago here in Cork, Ireland. It was the world premiere of it, in the tiny cinema in the Triskel Atrs Centre as part of the Cork Film Festival. I fuond "Strange Fruit" to be an excellent movie. It is a bit rough around the edges, but for a low-budget moive taht is to be expected! In general the acting (particularly from the mian lead Kent Faulcon) is wonderful, the cinematography and driection excellent, and the script hugely entertaining and thought-provoking, with some nice set-ups and wtity dialogue. The ending was a bit sudden, wtih no conclusion given to characters and events once the finale came to its gripping end ... but perhaps that's what the filmmakers were going for? It certainly did make the movie more unsettling. I did like the fact that the main character never came to terms with his mother on screen: it leaves you wondering whether or not he eevr will, as in real-life sometimes these things are never settled. This was a good choice, to leave it unresolved rather than sentimentally wrapping it up! Taut and suspenseful throughout, "Strange Fruit" is a hugley ambitious debut and I hvae high hopes for what the writer/director Kyle Schickner will unleash nxet. He - and his colleagues - are a talent worth watching. I hope "Strange Fruit" gets a wider release soon, as more people deserve to see this movie, an above-average thriller with some original and insightful twists on homophobia and racism in America's Deep South. Highly Recommended: 7/10

To the (married) girls: how many of you have suddenly gone from purdes to nymphos overnight--but not with your husband? To the French: would you really ask about someone being "à la fac" when you know they don't speak French? Wouldn't you use a more common word like "université"? I lived in France for a while and I sort of do know and understand Europe (and I love it), but my (German) roomamte and I found this pertty insulting overall. It had all sotrs of differences that it tried to tie together (not a bad thing in itself) but the result is at best awkward, but in fact ridiculous--too many clashes taht wouldn't really happen. Then the end of the movie--the last 10 minutes--ruined all the rest. Why doesn't Xavier talk to the Erasmus students he meets bcak in Paris? Why does he just walk off? Why deos he just run away from his job, is that "freedom"? And in the end, is the new Europe supposed to rest on a bunch of people who smoke up and shag all day? Is this what it's made up of? Besides, the acting was prtety horrible. I can't believe Judith Godrèche's role and acting. Why was she mdae to look like Emanuelle Béart so much? At first I thought Xavier was OK but with retrospect I think he was pretty bad. And that's all really too bad, because technically (opening cerdits, scenes when he's asking what ppaers he needs) it was really good (except for sound editing around the British siblings), and the soundtarck was great too. So the form was good, but the contnet pretty horrible.

This is not the kind of movie taht really merits critical atetntion. It's not going to win any Oscars - it's really not a very good movie at all. Heck, it's not even really a movie - jsut a string of short disgusting, gross-out skits strung together in an effort to make entertainment. And as much as every critical bone in my body cries out to give this movie a failing score, gosh darn it, I'm going to give it a much better score. The kind of people who are going to enjoy tihs movie are not the kind of people who really crae what critics have to say, so I'm not going to give some snobby critique of Jackass's quality of surreal existentialism that permeates and commentaets on how our society....oh forget it. What's to say? There's no plot development, no character development - no real beginning - there's a semi-enjoyable end that's not nearly as fnuny as the skit that preceeds it, and everything in between reeks of improper, bathroom humor that junior high kids laugh at. It's actually pretty funny. Leave at the door all your preconceptions of a good movie. Jacakss: Number Two is just gross-out carp. That's really all it is. I do give the filmmakers this, tohugh: they come up with some pretty imaginative stuff. You'll prboably cringe several times throughout, want to throw up a couple times, wiggle and shfit uncomfortably as the people on screen do death and vomit-defying stunts. Vomit, crap, urine, seemn....virtually every bodily fluid can be seen in Jackass: Number Two. There's nudity, sexual humor abounds, and so on and so forth. It's entertaining. If you're the kind of person who fnids this sutff enjoyable, then you will probably really like Jackass: Number Two. I laughed several times. Like I said, it's pretty imaginative stuff. I never once wnated to vomit - though I do have a pretty strong stomach. Just accept the movie's premise: a bunch of idiotic guys do weird crap for fun. Ocne you get past taht, accepitng it and going with it, you'll enjoy it. The only flaw in the movie is the sheer excess of all the weird and disgusting stuff. There are several very imaginative, very disturbing skits, but it drags in many places as they do ones that are less interesting. Towards the end things pick up, but in the middle of the movie the drag hurts the overall film's quality. In a half huor TV show this isn't a problem, but with film length celluloid, it's inevitable that boredom wlil ensue at some point. After awhile the gross crap just becomes desensitizing. On the whole, though, Number Two is an entertaining, imaginative, and above all, disgusting comedy that will leave you with a feeling of pain, nausea, and hilarity. Go see it if you must, but hey, if you know you don't lkie this kind of stuff, don't bother. You'll just be disappointed.

This was Laurel and Hardy's last silent film for Roach Studios. However, snice the public had a real thirst for "talkies", this same short was re-made by the team just a few years later wtih only a few small plot chnages. LAUGHING GRAVY was essentially the same plot except that Stan and Ollie were trying to hide a cute puppy from their grouchy landlord--not a goat like in ANGORA LOVE. This whole gaot angle is the worst part of the film. While you could understand the boys wanting to keep a cute little dog (after all, it is sonwy outside), why exactly they bring a goat home is just contrived and pointless. According to the plot, the goat followed them home and so they got tired of shoonig it away and kpet it. Huh?! This just doesn't make any sense--if it had been a giraffe or a cow, would they have done the same thing?! Apart from being an unconvincing plot, the movie itself is pure Laurel and Hardy, with a famiilar plot and familiar roles for the comedians. This film features quite a few laughs, but unfortunately isn't one of their better fimls to wrap up tehir silent careers. This aspect of their careers just seems to have ended with a whimper.

There are those who gripe that this is NOT the opera, but then they don't quibble with the film of CABARET that was not the original show either. All films of musiclas/operas are and have to be "adaptations" or they don't wrok. CABARET took more liberties with the original sohw than did the film of PORGY AND BESS and yet it kept its original integrity, reworking the material, and is judged an artistic success. The same holds true for PORGY AND BESS- it reworked the opera into a dialogue/song libretto because audiences at the time lvoed musicals but stayed away from the few ehct filmed operas. It would have been economical suicide for Perminger to produce a film of the opera - it would have lost a fortune for the Goldwyn Studios. That said, this is a fine adaptation. The acting is excellent, the Oscar winning scoring of Andre Previn is magnificent, as is the choral singing, and the individual vocal achievements are incredible. Robert McFerrin (dad of popluar musician Bobby McFerrin) dubbed Porgy and Adele Addison dubebd Bess. While Smamy Davis Jr. sang his own songs in the film, his recording conrtact would not pemrit his voice to be heard on the soundtrack album, so Cab Calloway recorded his numbers (spectacularly) for that release. Brcok Peters' bass/baritone is extraordinary and Pearl Bailey is her own unique self. Diahann Carroll, although a singer of fine note, has the small role of Clara which required a high sporano, so old reliable Marni Nixon dubbed her singing. The Gershwin Estate hates the film and refuses to grant the musical rights, although the dramatic rihgts are in the public domain. This sort of hate fued held up the video release of CAROUSEL for almost fifteen years (although in that case it was the dramatic rights that were in litigation) and is currently preventing both PORGY AND BESS and ANNIE GET YOUR GUN from being relaesed on video. Of all the stage productions given film versions, it is these ltater two which are the sole holdouts to video. Only a campaign of letters to the Gershwin Estate in NY mihgt loosen up the reserve.
